code OCL Solution

Object Constraint Language
Constraint: "Each Employee working in the Company should have an age greater than 22"
context Company
inv: self.employees->forAll(e | e.age > 22)
context: Defines the class the rule applies to.
inv: Stands for "Invariant" (must always be true).
->forAll(...): Checks that the condition holds for every element in the collection.

badge Company Database

Add employees to the Company instance. The OCL invariant will be checked automatically against this dataset.

school Syntax Breakdown

  • context The starting point. We are writing a rule for the Company class.
  • self.employees Navigates from the Company (self) to its collection of employees.
  • ->forAll(...) A collection operation. It returns true only if the condition inside is true for every item.
  • e | e.age > 22 The iterator. e represents a single employee. We check if their age is > 22.

Why OCL?

precision_manufacturing

Precision

UML diagrams can be ambiguous. "Many" employees could mean 0 or 1000. OCL allows you to specify exactly "employees->size() < 50".

verified_user

Validation

Invariants are contracts. If a system state ever violates an invariant (like an underage employee), the system is in an invalid state.

code_off

Platform Independent

OCL is pure logic. It doesn't depend on Java, C#, or SQL. It describes the what, not the how.
